overall: Washington DC is starting the day stuck at 75.2°F with a running max of only 77.0°F and essentially zero warming velocity — temperature has been flat since at least 04:52 ET. Skies are heavily overcast with 100% cloud fraction and a very low ceiling (~457m/1,500 ft), combined with a muggy dewpoint near 70°F and persistent east winds of 11-12 mph, all of which are suppressing typical morning solar heating. The day is running notably cooler than models suggested at this hour, though the peak is not expected until around 15:30-16:00 ET.
forecast_obs_notes: Models are meaningfully divergent: HRRR is the hot outlier at 87.4°F, GFS sits at 85.4°F, ECMWF at 82.5°F, and NBM is the most conservative at 80.8°F — a spread of nearly 7°F. The NWS narrative forecast of 84°F falls near the model mean (~84°F). The INTRADAY obs-driven model is bullishly skewed toward 88-92°F, but this appears inconsistent with the actual flat 75°F temperature trend and persistent low cloud deck as of 07:49 ET; the D1_NOW NWP-based model centering on 84-89°F seems more credible given current conditions.
max_temp_prediction: With clouds expected to thin later and the peak heating window still several hours away (forecast peak ~15:30 ET), a warm-up into the mid-to-upper 80s remains possible, but the heavy overcast and threat of afternoon convection (30% PoP, noon–5pm) introduce meaningful downside risk to that scenario. The NWS 84°F forecast aligns well with the GFS/ECMWF blend and the D1_NOW 84-85F bucket (23.6%), though the HRRR-driven 88-89F even bucket (36.7% per ensemble) can't be dismissed if skies break as expected. Confidence is moderate-low given model spread and the suppressive morning setup; best estimate is approximately 85°F, leaning toward the 84-85F even bucket but with real probability in the 86-89F range.
